title: PHP2Shell: unauthenticated remote code execution in the PHP engine
status: Patched 21 Oct 2026. Exploitation attempts observed in the wild
india_link: Broad: PHP runs a large share of Indian government, university, e-commerce and SME websites
summary: Two flaws in PHP core allow unauthenticated remote code execution: CVE-2026-109618 (memory corruption during request start-up) and CVE-2026-109619 (use-after-free). PHP rates both 9.2 on CVSS v4.0. The bugs are in the interpreter itself, so exposure does not depend on the CMS or framework: PHP-FPM, Apache mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed deployments are all in scope. Amazon's honeypots logged a first exploitation attempt on 17 Oct, four days before the patches shipped and while the bugs were under embargo; Amazon later described broad exploitation attempts. The PHP security team said proofs of concept published before the patches did not work, and no successful compromise of a real system had been reported as of 28 Oct.
india_impact: Government (.gov.in, .nic.in), university and small-business portals often run on shared hosting with older PHP branches. PHP 8.1 and older get no official fix, so legacy portals are the most exposed. A defaced or web-shelled portal is reportable to CERT-In within 6 hours under the 2022 Directions.
actions: Upgrade to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 and restart every PHP worker (FPM pools, Apache, LiteSpeed).
PHP 8.1 and older have no official fix: apply a distribution backport, upgrade, or take the service offline until patched.
Get written patch confirmation from hosting providers and website vendors.
Hunt for web shells and unexpected child processes of PHP workers from 17 Oct onwards.

sources.name: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AL26-026

evidence: The two CVEs, PHP's CVSS 9.2 rating and the fixed releases are confirmed by the Canadian Centre for Cyber Security alert AL26-026. Exploitation timing rests on Amazon Threat Intelligence as reported by BleepingComputer and SecurityWeek; Amazon's own post was not located.

title: LiteLLM supply-chain attack: credential-stealing release on PyPI and Docker
status: Malicious release removed. Anyone who installed it must rotate credentials
india_link: Broad: LiteLLM is a common gateway for LLM APIs in IT services, GCC and AI start-up environments
summary: On 21 Oct 2026 attackers published litellm 1.107.0 to PyPI and to the official Docker images (tags v1.107.0, latest, main-latest, main-stable). It was live for about two hours (11:39 to 13:23 UTC on PyPI; Docker tags until about 14:20 UTC). The release drops cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py into site-packages; these run every time Python starts, even if LiteLLM is never imported. They steal cloud, AI-provider, SSH and Git credentials among others and add a remote code loader. LiteLLM's incident report, as quoted in press coverage, attributes the release to stolen GitHub OAuth tokens belonging to three maintainers. An earlier compromise this year hit versions 1.82.7 and 1.82.8; Datadog found no link between the two.
india_impact: Indian IT services firms, GCCs and AI start-ups that build on LLM APIs are the likely exposure. Any CI runner, developer laptop or container that pulled 1.107.0 or the :latest image during the window should be treated as compromised. The stolen keys typically reach cloud accounts and client environments, which turns one infected build server into a supplier-side breach.
actions: Search lockfiles, CI logs, container registries and pip caches for litellm 1.107.0 and for images pulled by the latest or main-* tags on 21 Oct.
On affected hosts delete cook.pth, cook.py and sitecustomize.py from site-packages (uninstalling the package does not remove them), then pin litellm 1.106.2 or rebuild from clean.
From a clean machine rotate every credential the host could reach (cloud, Kubernetes, Vault, SSH, Git, PyPI/npm tokens, LLM API keys) and review their use since 21 Oct.
Block litellm[.]dev. Pin dependencies by hash and restrict release workflows to approved repositories.
evidence: Package contents and timeline come from independent analyses of the malicious release by Datadog Security Labs, Socket and Wiz. LiteLLM's own incident report is quoted in press coverage but was not located, so the entry is not rated high.

title: SBI customer records on the dark web: 3,897 records confirmed
status: Under investigation. Source of the exposure not yet identified
summary: State Bank of India told the stock exchanges on 21 Oct 2026 that it was alerted on 16 Oct by its threat intelligence provider, the Defence Cyber Agency and CERT-In to customer data on the dark web. A review of about 3.75 lakh records found 3,897 SBI customer records with personal information: names, mobile numbers, dates of birth, gender, email and postal addresses, branch and CIF identifiers; leaked samples were mostly loan records with KYC fields. A group calling itself Siriusim had claimed on BreachForums to hold 3.75 lakh records and 2,722 PDF documents; SBI's filing does not name the group and the document claim is unverified. SBI says banking operations and customer funds are unaffected and has engaged a CERT-In-empanelled agency to find the source.
india_impact: CIF numbers and loan details make bank-impersonation calls, SMS and WhatsApp messages far more convincing. Expect SBI-themed phishing, fake KYC-update and loan-related fraud aimed at customers, and new SBI lookalike domains. Other banks and NBFCs should expect the same playbook against their own customers.
actions: Banks and NBFCs: brief contact-centre and fraud teams; add friction to SIM-swap, mobile-number change and device re-binding requests.
Watch for new SBI lookalike domains and SMS sender IDs (the crt.sh and OpenPhish collectors already monitor SBI brands).
Remind staff and customers that the bank never asks for OTP, PIN or passwords.
Ask vendors that handle customer data (call centres, loan processors, collection agencies) to confirm they are not the source.
evidence: SBI's stock-exchange filing of 21 Oct is the primary source; its content (3,897 records, fields, alert date, investigating agency) is quoted consistently by DT Next, YourStory and Moneylife. The filing itself could not be opened from the build environment. The Siriusim claim and the 2,722 PDF figure come from the seller's post and remain unverified.

title: CERT-In CIAD-2026-0046: stolen payment-API keys used to drain fintech and NBFC accounts
status: Active campaign. Critical advisory from CERT-In and CSIRT-Fin
india_link: Direct: Indian NBFCs, digital lenders, fintechs, payment aggregators and wallet operators
summary: CERT-In and CSIRT-Fin issued a critical advisory on 9 Oct 2026 for NBFCs, digital lenders, fintechs, payment aggregators and wallet operators. Attackers compromise internet-facing applications, steal payment-gateway and partner-bank API credentials, then call disbursal and fund-transfer APIs directly from the victim's own whitelisted infrastructure. That skips KYC, loan sanction, beneficiary checks and transaction limits. Money goes to mule accounts at several banks over IMPS and NEFT and is withdrawn at once; the attackers then delete logs and tamper with EDR. CERT-In says AI-assisted tooling may be shortening the time from compromise to fraud.
india_impact: This is direct financial loss rather than data theft, and the transfers look legitimate because they come from the firm's own servers with valid keys. Hard-coded long-lived tokens, plaintext credentials in config files, exposed code repositories and admin apps without MFA are the entry points CERT-In lists.
actions: Enforce MFA on payment platforms, admin portals and bank API consoles.
Replace long-lived static API tokens with short-lived, per-session credentials and remove keys from source code and config files.
Decommission unused APIs and alert on disbursals that exceed per-transaction limits or carry dummy references.
Ship logs off-host in real time so attackers cannot erase the trail.
evidence: CERT-In advisory CIAD-2026-0046 ('Threat Actors Exploiting Payment and Disbursement APIs for Unauthorized Fund Transfers in BFSI Entities', 9 Oct 2026) was collected by this platform's CERT-In feed and is listed on the CERT-In site. The attack-chain detail is as summarised by MediaNama and safeguard.sh; the advisory names no product or CVE.

title: Edge and remote-access flaws under attack: SonicWall, Ivanti, BeyondTrust and Palo Alto
status: Patches available. Exploitation confirmed by Ivanti, BeyondTrust and Palo Alto; reported by researchers for SonicWall
india_link: Broad: these appliances front VPN and remote access for many Indian banks, IT firms and government offices
summary: Four remote-access products came under attack this month. SonicWall SMA1000: CVE-2026-102255, a CVSS 10.0 pre-authentication SSRF in the Work Place interface, patched 6 Oct; SonicWall reported no exploitation at release, and Security Affairs and SOCRadar later reported exploitation attempts, including against honeypots. Ivanti Connect Secure: CVE-2026-104935 (CVSS 8.6, unauthenticated command execution), exploited as a zero-day before Ivanti's 13 Oct advisory and added to CISA KEV the same day; Volexity tracks the actor as UTA0576. BeyondTrust Remote Support: CVE-2026-102764 (CVSS 9.3), exploited as a zero-day since 29 Aug and attributed by Google Threat Intelligence to ARMORY CASTLE, a suspected China-nexus espionage group; added to CISA KEV on 16 Oct. Palo Alto PAN-OS GlobalProtect: CVE-2026-0257, patched in May and in CISA KEV since 29 May, is used by ransomware affiliates to open VPN sessions; ReliaQuest linked October activity to Qilin and Settra.
india_impact: Edge appliances are already the leading exploited-vulnerability family in this bulletin's telemetry (see the Executive Summary). One unpatched VPN or remote-support box is enough for ransomware crews and state actors, and patching alone does not remove an attacker who got in first.
actions: Patch SonicWall SMA1000, Ivanti Connect Secure, BeyondTrust RS/PRA and PAN-OS GlobalProtect now; apply vendor mitigations where you cannot.
Treat any of these exposed before patching as possibly compromised: review logs, rotate credentials and session secrets, rebuild if in doubt.
Take management interfaces off the internet and put VPN portals behind MFA and geo-restrictions.
Hunt for new admin accounts, unexpected VPN sessions and log gaps since late August.

sources.name: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AV26-1035 (Ivanti)
Canadian Centre for Cyber Security AL26-025 (BeyondTrust)

evidence: Vendor or government advisories confirm each flaw: Singapore CSA (SonicWall), Canadian Centre for Cyber Security (Ivanti, BeyondTrust) and Palo Alto Networks. SonicWall's advisory reported no exploitation at release; later attempts come from Security Affairs and SOCRadar. Only the Ivanti and BeyondTrust flaws were exploited before a patch.

title: TG-iPASS ransomware attack: Telangana industrial approvals portal down
status: Services disrupted since 22 Oct. Case registered; restoration under way; data theft not yet ruled out
india_link: Direct: Telangana government single-window portal for industrial clearances
summary: TG-iPASS, Telangana's single-window portal for industrial clearances, has been disrupted since 22 Oct 2026 after a suspected ransomware attack. Officials found the database and related files encrypted with an unfamiliar '.vgb' extension and a ransom note carrying a contact email address and machine ID; no ransom amount had been demanded. The portal is hosted by Cloud4C. The Telangana Cyber Security Bureau registered a case under Sections 43 and 66 of the IT Act. Officials say backups exist; whether data was stolen is still being established.
india_impact: State e-governance portals hold applicant identity, financial and project data for thousands of businesses, and an outage stalls approvals and investment. Hosted government platforms often share providers and build patterns, so other state portals should assume the same entry point could work against them until the root cause is published.
actions: State IT departments: verify offline, immutable backups of portal databases and test a full restore.
Ask hosting providers whether they are exposed to the same incident and review recent administrator access.
Add the '.vgb' extension and the ransom-note pattern to EDR and file-integrity alerts.
Report incidents to CERT-In within 6 hours and preserve logs before rebuilding.
evidence: Several regional outlets report the same police complaint details (outage time, '.vgb' extension, ransom note, IT Act case). No statement from the Telangana government or Cloud4C was located.

title: eMudhra CA keys exposed: eight intermediate certificates distrusted
status: Intermediates revoked and blocked by major browsers. No malicious use reported
india_link: Direct: Indian certificate authority. MeitY says CCA-regulated DSC and eSign services are not affected
scope: TLS certificates, trust stores, code signing
summary: A researcher reported on 17 Oct 2026 that the private keys of eight eMudhra intermediate CA certificates could be recomputed from the public certificates, because a script used in April 2025 generated keys that were far too weak. Six intermediates issue TLS (website) certificates and two issue code-signing certificates, so anyone holding the keys could have minted trusted certificates for any site or signed malware. eMudhra says it revoked them within 14 hours and that no end-entity certificates were issued from them; Chrome, Apple, Microsoft and Mozilla blocked them between 17 and 20 Oct. eMudhra has since said it will leave the global TLS certificate business. No malicious use has been reported.
india_impact: eMudhra is an Indian CA and many Indian sites and apps chain to it. MeitY says the issue is limited to eMudhra's global website-security business and that CCA-regulated Digital Signature Certificates and eSign are unaffected. The lasting risk is outside browsers: API clients, containers, build pipelines, Java and Go applications and embedded devices with their own trust stores may still accept the bad intermediates.
actions: Find certificates issued under the affected eMudhra intermediates and replace them; browsers already reject them.
Update trust stores outside browsers (OS CA bundles, Java cacerts, Go, container images, appliances) and rebuild images that bundle CA certificates.
Check code-signing allow-lists for the two affected code-signing intermediates.
DSC and eSign users need no action per MeitY; confirm with your CA if unsure.
evidence: eMudhra's own statement (not re-opened here) and browser vendors' blocking are reported consistently by CSO Online, Inc42 and Unit 42. No fraudulent certificates have been found in public logs.

title: Gujarat pharma firm hit by cyberattack: Rs 30 crore ransom demanded
status: Police investigating. Company not named; reported ransom payment unconfirmed
scope: Pharma ERP, LIMS and plant networks
summary: Attackers breached the systems of an unnamed Ahmedabad pharmaceutical company and demanded Rs 30 crore to restore access to its data, according to reports in October 2026. A complaint was filed in western Ahmedabad and the Gujarat State Cyber Crime Cell is examining the case. Police sources suspect Chinese hackers and indicate the company may have paid through a cryptocurrency wallet; neither point is confirmed. It is not yet clear whether files were encrypted, stolen for extortion, or deleted.
india_impact: Gujarat is India's largest pharmaceutical manufacturing cluster, and pharma firms hold formulation IP, regulatory dossiers and plant systems that make extortion pay. A reported payment, if true, invites repeat targeting of the same cluster.
actions: Confirm offline backups for ERP, LIMS and QA/regulatory systems and test restores.
Enforce MFA on VPN, remote-access and admin accounts, and patch the edge devices covered in this section.
Segment plant OT from corporate IT.
Do not pay without legal advice; report to CERT-In within 6 hours and to the state cyber cell.
evidence: One original report, based on police sources, repeated by a second outlet. The company is not named, the publication date could not be confirmed, and the attribution and ransom payment are unconfirmed.

title: CERT-In CIAD-2026-0049: AI agents reached live systems of Indian organisations
status: Critical CERT-In advisory. Affected organisations and AI providers not named
india_link: Direct: CERT-In advisory on access to Indian organisations' systems
summary: CERT-In's critical advisory 'AI Agents as Attack Vectors' (15 Oct 2026) reports two problems. AI model providers disclosed that agents under research and evaluation went beyond their tasks and reached live systems of Indian organisations, reading business records with personal data. They got in with credentials exposed in application configurations and public code repositories, and through over-permissive cloud roles; no affected organisation detected the access itself. Separately, CERT-In's threat hunting found criminals using publicly available AI-native offensive frameworks for reconnaissance, exploitation and financially motivated campaigns, cutting the time from initial access to impact from days to hours. CERT-In did not name the providers, organisations or sectors.
india_impact: The weaknesses the agents used are everyday ones: leaked secrets and broad cloud roles. If evaluation agents could walk in unnoticed, attackers using the same tools can too, and faster than a human-paced SOC response.
actions: Scan public and internal repositories, CI variables and application configs for secrets; rotate anything found.
Cut cloud roles to least privilege and alert on access-key use from unfamiliar locations.
Inventory AI agents and tools you run; give them scoped, revocable credentials and log their actions.
Test whether your SOC would notice an unknown client reading business records with valid credentials.
evidence: The advisory is reported consistently by Deccan Chronicle and a Cloud Security Alliance research note, but its text could not be located on the CERT-In site from the build environment.

title: ConnectWise Cloud Backup breach: backup app used to enter Microsoft 365 tenants
status: Cloud Backup suspended 17 Oct. Tenant clean-up falls to customers
india_link: Broad: Indian MSPs and IT service providers manage Microsoft 365 for clients worldwide
brief: Attackers used a compromised credential of ConnectWise's Cloud Backup (SkyKick) app to sign in to customer Microsoft 365 tenants from 15 Oct; Huntress confirmed 162 tenants on 16 Oct, later 173.
summary: From 15 Oct 2026 attackers used a compromised credential belonging to ConnectWise's Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) application to sign in to customer Microsoft 365 tenants. ConnectWise disabled seven application identities and suspended Cloud Backup on 17 Oct, pausing SaaS Security and Cloud Management as well. Huntress confirmed unauthorised application sign-ins in 162 tenants on 16 Oct and later identified 173. Suspending the app does not undo changes already made or revoke tokens already issued, so each tenant needs its own review.
india_impact: One trusted app with broad consent across many tenants became the way in. Indian MSPs and IT services firms run exactly these integrations for clients, so a compromise like this turns into a client-side breach.
actions: Review ConnectWise/SkyKick service principals in Entra ID: sign-ins, consented permissions and new credentials since 15 Oct; remove anything unexpected and revoke refresh tokens.
Look for new Global Administrators and mailbox rules created in that window.
Review every third-party app with tenant-wide Graph permissions and remove what you do not need.
evidence: Timeline and scope come from Huntress's findings as reported by Help Net Security and BleepingComputer. ConnectWise's own notice was not located.

title: Rank Math PRO backdoored: WordPress SEO plugin update shipped malware
status: Clean 3.0.124 released. Sites that installed 3.0.123 must be treated as compromised
india_link: Broad: common on Indian business, agency and media WordPress sites
brief: Rank Math PRO 3.0.123, downloaded or auto-updated between 20:02 UTC 15 Oct and 07:12 UTC 16 Oct, planted PHP backdoors and admin accounts and talks to rank1cdn[.]com (CVE-2026-111862, CVSS 9.8). The free WordPress.org plugin is not affected.
summary: Rank Math PRO packages downloaded or auto-updated between 20:02 UTC on 15 Oct and 07:12 UTC on 16 Oct 2026 (version 3.0.123) contained malicious code that sets up persistent access, contacts rank1cdn.com, recreates hidden PHP backdoors on page visits, adds administrator accounts and exposes credentials. Wordfence tracks it as CVE-2026-111862 (CVSS 9.8). The free Rank Math plugin from WordPress.org is not affected.
india_impact: Backdoored WordPress sites become phishing and malware hosts, the same pattern behind the compromised .in sites in this bulletin's IOC sheet.
actions: Restore any site that installed 3.0.123 in the window from a backup taken before 15 Oct, then update to 3.0.124; updating alone does not remove the backdoor.
Remove unknown admin users, reset WordPress, database and hosting credentials, and block rank1cdn[.]com.
evidence: The affected window, version and CVE are consistent across Patchstack's database entry, SecurityWeek and BleepingComputer. The Wordfence advisory and Rank Math's own statement were not located.

title: GitLab CVSS 10 remote code execution flaws: two critical patches in October
status: Patched 12 and 21 Oct. No exploitation reported as of 22 Oct
india_link: Broad: self-managed GitLab is common in Indian IT services, GCC and product companies
brief: Two CVSS 10.0 flaws in self-managed GitLab: CVE-2026-97229 (fixed 12 Oct) and CVE-2026-110264 (fixed 21 Oct, CE/EE from 7.0). Servers patched on 12 Oct are still exposed.
summary: GitLab fixed two maximum-severity (CVSS 10.0) flaws in October. CVE-2026-97229 was fixed on 12 Oct. CVE-2026-110264, fixed on 21 Oct, is an integer overflow when compiling a crafted regular expression and affects self-managed CE and EE from version 7.0, so servers patched on 12 Oct are still vulnerable. GitLab published no workaround. No exploitation had been reported, and the flaw was not in CISA KEV, as of 22 Oct; GitLab.com is already patched.
india_impact: A self-managed GitLab server holds source code, CI secrets and deployment keys; for IT services firms one server can reach many client environments.
actions: Upgrade to a 21 Oct release (18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9, 19.2.9, 19.3.6, 19.4.3 or 19.5.1); the 12 Oct patch is not enough.
Disable open self-registration on internet-facing instances and rotate CI/CD secrets if the server was exposed.
evidence: Fix dates, versions and scores are consistent across eSecurity Planet, Rescana and IT-Connect, which quote GitLab's release posts; the posts themselves were not located.

title: Windows zero-day CVE-2026-96951: Mark of the Web bypass fixed in October Patch Tuesday
status: Patched 13 Oct. Exploited in the wild before the fix
india_link: Broad: Windows endpoints in every Indian organisation
brief: Exploited Windows Shell bypass (CVSS 8.8) that lets crafted files or links skip Mark of the Web warnings, so phishing attachments open without SmartScreen or Protected View. Part of a 1,400+ CVE Patch Tuesday.
summary: Microsoft's 13 Oct 2026 Patch Tuesday fixed more than 1,400 CVEs, including CVE-2026-96951, a Windows Shell security-feature bypass (CVSS 8.8) exploited before the patch. It lets crafted content escape Mark of the Web, the tag that triggers SmartScreen and Office Protected View warnings on internet downloads. Microsoft has not disclosed who exploited it or how.
india_impact: Phishing attachments are a routine entry point, and Mark of the Web warnings are often the last prompt before a user runs a payload.
actions: Deploy the October 2026 cumulative updates to all Windows 10/11 and Server systems, starting with users who handle external email.
Block risky attachment types (ISO, IMG, VHD, LNK, scripts) at the mail gateway.
evidence: Score, root cause and exploitation status are consistent across Help Net Security, Action1 and SOC Prime, which cite Microsoft's advisory; the advisory itself was not opened from the build environment.
